# A Canadian Smoking Histories Model: A Study Protocol

Version 0.3.2

Date: 2026-09-22

Corresponds to full protocol v0.4.5. This summary is versioned independently.

## Purpose

The Canadian Smoking Histories Model (CSHM) will describe smoking patterns by birth cohort, sex and province or territory, with historical reporting planned for 1965--2024 and status quo projections to 2050. It extends the US smoking-history approach and its Ontario adaptation to support Canadian population health modelling, including OncoSim and POHEM.

## Data

The study plans to use Canadian Community Health Survey (CCHS) cycles from 2001--2024, subject to source-specific availability and analysis eligibility. Development and independently reproducible public-data analyses use public-use microdata files (PUMFs) through 2022. The 2019--2020 and 2022 PUMFs contribute cross-sectional prevalence only because their age groups are too broad for annual history reconstruction. Definitive estimates use Master files in authorized environments at Statistics Canada headquarters or Research Data Centres. Master files retain more detail where it was collected, but do not always provide exact smoking-history timing.

## Methods

Following Holford et al. [@Holford_AJPM_2014] and Manuel et al. [@Manuel_HR_2020], sex-specific age-period-cohort models will estimate initiation and cessation. The three smoking states are never, current and former. Among respondents who have smoked at least 100 cigarettes, initiation is dated at the first whole cigarette. Cessation means stopping completely for at least two years at survey; a one-year definition is a sensitivity analysis. Daily and occasional smoking remain descriptive and intensity characteristics within this framework.

The cchsflow package will harmonize inputs. Item non-response will be handled by chained-equations multiple imputation. Observed grouped complete-cessation durations will use interval-constrained multiple imputation, deriving smoking state, quit timing and risk history consistently within each completed dataset. Distributions, feasible bounds and uncertainty pooling require specification and validation before use. PUMF imputation will not be calibrated using Master data.

Canadian risk time begins at arrival, subject to age and risk-set rules; earlier smoking exposure remains relevant to lifetime dose. The reviewed Master questions record arrival through 2014, landed-immigrant year in 2015--2021, and both in 2022--2023. PUMF residence durations are grouped; status categories include non-permanent residents from 2015--2016. Direct arrival will be used where available; the treatment of observations without it remains a specific analytical decision. Racial-group predictors for imputation must respect changes in the underlying classifications.

MPoRT is the planned primary mortality adjustment, with a Peto-method sensitivity analysis. Mortality inputs may come from either Statistics Canada or the Canadian Human Mortality Database. The adjustment estimator and selected source coverage will be recorded before analysis. Until implemented and validated, unadjusted outputs describe survey survivors.

## Validation and outputs

Validation will include CCHS cycles held out from fitting. Uncertainty will combine imputation and survey variation, using CCHS bootstrap weights for Master analyses and explicitly approximate methods for PUMFs. Planned outputs include rate tables, synthetic smoking histories, an open-source implementation and an interactive platform. The protocol remains a review draft: APC settings, intensity methods, immigration timing, national aggregation and selected sensitivity analyses require further decisions before final analysis.

## Change log

Version 0.3.2. Date: 2026-09-22. Corresponds to full protocol v0.4.5: replaces broad exposure-source audit placeholders with documented immigration definitions and complete-cessation routing. Distinguishes source validation from the remaining migration and event-time imputation decisions.

Version 0.3.1. Date: 2026-09-22. Corresponds to full protocol v0.4.4: updates planned coverage through 2024, grouped quit-duration imputation, independent PUMF execution, source-specific eligibility, immigration and racial-group limitations, secure analysis locations and the choice of mortality source. Corrects the earlier attribution of the Canadian model to the US National Cancer Institute.

Version 0.3.0. Date: 2026-08-07. Corresponds to full protocol v0.4.0 (methodological amendments following external review and adjudication): named the three smoking states and transition definitions (initiation at first whole cigarette; cessation as stopping completely); identified APC parameterization stated explicitly; uncertainty via CCHS bootstrap replicate weights in the Master-file analysis; validation language corrected from cross-survey calibration to within-CCHS validation with held-out cycles.

Version 0.2.0. Date: 2026-06-15. Refreshed to correspond to full protocol v0.3.2: corrected the harmonization appendix reference (Appendix A) and aligned terminology (CSHM, OncoSim). No change to study scope or methods.

Version 0.1.0. Date: 2025-03-27. Initial 1-page outline.
